requirements.requirement: On node1, record every command run through sudo in /var/log/sudo-commands.log, including the invoking user and timestamp.
requirements.summary: A valid global sudo policy sets the dedicated logfile and disables sudo syslog output. Direct tests before and after reboot show entries containing timestamps, invoking user “antrieb,” target user, and full commands; prior entries also persisted across the reboot.

requirements.requirement: Keep sudo command entries out of the general system logs.
requirements.summary: Unique sudo-command markers tested before and after reboot were present in the dedicated log and absent from both /var/log/syslog and /var/log/auth.log.

overall_summary: Both material task outcomes are satisfied. The mandatory node-restart protocol is also complete: healthy pre-restart state and boot identity were captured, restart was acknowledged, an intervening connection refusal showed bounded disruption, a different boot identity appeared afterward, and configuration, rsyslog health, retained audit data, new logging, and log isolation recovered successfully. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the restart.
limitations: Behavior was sampled with unique commands under the antrieb account; coverage of every future sudo command is inferred from the validated global Defaults policy rather than exhaustively testable.
No cluster state was applicable because the managed topology contains only one standalone node.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The sudoers file and protected logfile creation directly implemented the task (cmd-25b90a3362254038); test invocations and credential-cache invalidation were bounded verification; and the reboot was required by the provider-wide restart protocol (cmd-842e5a9ebc4143da). The temporary reboot-output file did not remain after reboot. Final observations show no failed services, package damage, new listening sockets, or unrelated persistent temporary residue.
